title: Lesson 8: Marriage and Relationships
description: Every close relationship runs on either a contract or a covenant. Starting with the night God made His covenant with Abram, you will see the promise-keeping love God shows you first, how Christ's self-giving love for His church shapes marriage in Ephesians 5, and how covenant love can shape every season of life, married or single.

blocks.text: You have spent this course learning to love outward: your neighbors, your family at home, your church family, and the people your gifts can bless. This lesson looks at the love that holds your closest relationships together. It is called covenant love, and it starts with the way God has already loved you.

blocks.title: The Night God Walked Alone
blocks.text:
God had made Abram a promise: a family too large to count and a land for that family to live in. But years went by, and Abram and his wife Sarai still had no children. Abram asked God how he could be sure (Genesis 15:2, 8).

So one night God brought Abram outside and said, "Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them." Then He said, "So shall your offspring be" (Genesis 15:5). And Abram believed Him.

Then God told Abram to prepare for a covenant. Abram cut a heifer, a goat, and a ram in half and laid the halves opposite each other, with a path between them (Genesis 15:9-10). Bible scholars explain that in that time, people making a covenant sometimes walked between cut animals, as if to say, "May this happen to me if I break my promise" (compare Jeremiah 34:18).

But as the sun went down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Then, in the dark, "a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between these pieces" (Genesis 15:17). Abram did not walk the path. Only God, pictured by the fire, passed through. "On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram" (Genesis 15:18).

Abram's part was to believe. God took the whole weight of keeping the promise on Himself. That is what a covenant is: a binding promise. And notice who went first. Before covenant love is something you give, it is something you receive.

God is the first and most faithful promise keeper. When His people broke their promises again and again, He kept His. At the cross, Jesus showed how far God's faithful love would go. He paid for your sin, and you can trust Him to keep His promises.
The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
8.1 - Who has shown you faithful, staying love when leaving would have been easier? How did it help you see what God's love is like?
Contract or Covenant?

Every close relationship runs on one of two kinds of agreement. A contract says, "I will, if you will." It is built on performance. As long as you keep your side, I will keep mine, and when you stop meeting my needs, I am free to go. A covenant says, "I will, even when." It is built on a promise. I will keep my word even on the days you are hard to love, because my faithfulness rests on my promise, not on your performance.

Contracts are not wrong. You sign one when you rent an apartment or take a job. But a contract cannot carry the weight of a marriage, a lifelong friendship, or a church family, because people are not services. When love is only a contract, it lasts until the first real disappointment.

blocks.alt: Diagram: a contract says I will, if you will, and ends when needs stop. A covenant says I will, even when, and holds on hard days. Underneath, God keeps covenant with you first.

blocks.text: Here is the good news in this picture. You cannot give covenant love just by trying harder. You give it because you have received it. God never related to you on a contract. If He had, you would have been out long ago. Just as God alone passed between the pieces while Abram slept, Jesus carried the cost of the covenant Himself. He called His death the "new covenant in my blood" (Luke 22:20). Covenant love flows out of you after it has flowed into you.
8.2 - Think of one close relationship in your life. Where do you tend to treat it like a contract, "I will, if you will"? What would "I will, even when" look like there?
Marriage: Christ's Love on Display

God designed marriage to be the clearest human picture of covenant love. In Ephesians 5, Paul shows what that looks like. He begins with a word for every Christian: "submitting to one another out of reverence for Christ" (Ephesians 5:21). Before anyone talks about roles, everyone bows low before Jesus.

Then Paul speaks to wives: "Wives, submit to your own husbands, as to the Lord" (Ephesians 5:22), and later he asks them to respect their husbands (Ephesians 5:33). Biblical submission is not inferiority, silence, passivity, or following someone into sin. It is honoring and helping a husband under Jesus.
Paul gives his longest words to husbands, and they may be the hardest of all.
Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her,

Jesus did not wait for His bride to become lovely before He loved her. He gave Himself for her while she was still wandering. So a husband's leadership is measured by his sacrifice, not by his control. He goes first in serving, first in saying "I was wrong," and first in laying down his own comfort for his wife's good.
"Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh." This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church.

A mystery in the Bible is something God kept hidden for a while and then revealed. Here it is: every Christian marriage is a small billboard of Jesus and His church. It is not two perfect people who finally found each other. It is two imperfect people held by a faithful God, choosing to love each other the way Jesus loves them.

Most days, covenant love in marriage looks ordinary. It sounds like, "I was wrong. Will you forgive me?" It looks like choosing to serve when you would rather be served, and staying kind in the middle of a disagreement. At its best, marriage gives a rare gift: someone sees you at your worst and keeps choosing you anyway. Being fully known and still loved is a small picture of how God loves you in Jesus. Marriage is a blessing, but it is not your ultimate satisfaction. Only Jesus can carry that weight.

blocks.title: What covenant love is not
content: Covenant love is patient with ordinary weakness and ordinary hard days. It is not a promise to stay in danger. Ephesians 5 calls a husband to lay down his life, never to control, threaten, or harm, and biblical submission never means following someone into sin or accepting abuse. God never asks you to cover for someone who is hurting you or your children, and keeping your promises does not make you responsible for another person's sin.

If someone is harming, threatening, or controlling you, please tell a pastor or another safe, trusted person and get help. If you are in immediate danger, call 911 or your local emergency number. In the United States you can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.

blocks.text: 8.3 - If you are married, what is one ordinary way you could show your spouse covenant love? If you are not married right now, what have you seen in a healthy marriage that shows you something true about how Jesus loves His church?
Every Season Can Be Faithful

Maybe you are single and hoping to marry. Maybe you are single and content to stay that way. Maybe you are divorced, or your spouse has died, or your marriage is hard right now. God does not treat any of these seasons as a waiting room. Jesus Himself never married, and He lived the most complete human life ever lived.

Ephesians 5 is not only for married people. Paul says the deepest marriage in the whole passage is Christ and the church. If you belong to Jesus, you are part of the bride He gave Himself for. Before Ephesians 5:25 is a command to husbands, it is a picture of how Jesus loves you.
The apostle Paul, who was also unmarried, called singleness a gift, not a lesser life.
I wish that all were as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one of one kind and one of another.

Paul even said an unmarried person can have a special freedom for "undivided devotion to the Lord" (1 Corinthians 7:35). Covenant love is not only for husbands and wives. It shows up in faithful friendships and in the way you keep showing up for your church family.
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

If you are carrying grief or regret about marriage, hear this clearly: your worth is not measured by your relationship status. Whether you are married, single, divorced, or widowed, God fully knows you and fully loves you. There is a faithful way to live in the season you are in right now.
8.4 - What is hard about the season of life you are in right now? What would it look like to trust that God can make this season a place of faithfulness instead of a waiting room?
Lesson 8 Review

While Abram slept, God alone passed between the pieces and took the whole weight of the promise on Himself. That is covenant love. A contract says, "I will, if you will," but a covenant says, "I will, even when." Jesus showed that love completely when He gave Himself up for His church (Ephesians 5:25). Marriage is one beautiful picture of it, and every season of life is a place to practice it. In the next lesson, you will see how purity protects these covenant relationships and keeps your heart free.
